name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,294

entries.clue: Performer caught out at first by microphone (5)

indicatorNotes.at first: what comes at first in a word is its opening letter, so only the O of 'out' is taken
indicatorNotes.by: one thing placed by another sits beside it, so the pieces run on side by side

blocks.note: c = caught, the cricket scorecard abbreviation
first letter of 'out'
microphone clipped to its first three letters, the everyday short form

annotation.surface: A stand-up act is ambushed by the microphone before the show even starts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Caught out' reads as one phrase, but 'caught' gives C by itself and 'out at first' gives just the O.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a comic is a comedian, someone who stands on stage telling jokes, and so one kind of entertainer.

entries.clue: Coin dispatched to be picked up (4)

indicatorNotes.to be picked up: a sound is picked up by the ear or a microphone, so the word is heard rather than seen

blocks.note: dispatched means posted off; say that word aloud and respell it

annotation.surface: A coin is sent off in the post to be collected at the other end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' suggests collecting the coin, but here it means heard: SENT and CENT sound the same.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the cent is the small copper piece worth one hundredth of a dollar or euro.

entries.clue: Note characters turning up during home matches (4)

indicatorNotes.turning up: in a down answer, turning up means reading from the bottom to the top
indicatorNotes.during: something that happens during an event sits inside it, so the letters lie within the phrase that follows

blocks.note: sitting inside h(OME M)atches

annotation.surface: A note records which players showed up for the home games.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Characters' simply means letters: the answer is made of characters found in 'home matches', read upward.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a memo, short for memorandum, is a brief written message passed round an office.

entries.clue: Cheat with writing one’s made to join up (9)

blocks.note: to con is to cheat
script = handwriting

annotation.surface: Someone forges documents to get into the army.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase describing a person rather than a single word; 'join up' means enlist.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: a conscript is drafted into military service by law rather than volunteering.

entries.clue: News articles beginning to slate Conservatives (7)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the S of 'slate' is used

blocks.note: first letter of 'slate'
Tories is the nickname for Britain's Conservative Party

annotation.surface: The papers open by laying into the Conservative government.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Slate' here is British for criticise harshly, which makes the surface a press attack; in the wordplay it only supplies S.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: journalists call each piece they file a story, so the plural covers a paper's reports.

entries.clue: Witness was lying about up-and-down affair (6)

indicatorNotes.lying about: something lying about has been turned round, so WAS lies the other way

blocks.note: to witness is to see
used as it stands, then turned around

annotation.surface: A witness gave false evidence about an on-off relationship.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Was lying' looks like perjury, but 'lying about' just flips WAS; 'affair' is not romantic but a thing that goes up and down.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: a playground plank pivoting in the middle, each end rising as the other falls.

entries.clue: Djokovic, maybe, neither starting nor finishing eggs (3)

indicatorNotes.neither starting nor finishing: a word that neither starts nor finishes has lost its first and last letters

blocks.note: Novak Djokovic, the Serbian tennis player; 'maybe' flags that it is one Novak among many
N and K are dropped

annotation.surface: A tennis star neither starts nor finishes his eggs at breakfast.
annotation.walkthrough: The surname points you to the first name: Djokovic is Novak, and only the middle survives.
annotation.definitionFit: Latin plural: ova are egg cells, the word biologists use for the female reproductive cell.

entries.clue: Personal letters? (8)

blocks.note: the surface reads this as private, but it means belonging to a particular person
not correspondence but characters of the alphabet

annotation.walkthrough: 'Personal letters' sounds like private correspondence; the question mark warns that the letters are alphabet letters belonging to a person.
annotation.definitionFit: Cryptic reading: the capitals that begin your first name and surname are the letters peculiar to you.

entries.clue: Scot lacking heart to encourage SNP politician (8)

indicatorNotes.lacking heart: the heart of a word is its middle, so SCOT loses its central CO

blocks.note: SCOT without its middle CO
to urge on is to encourage

annotation.surface: A heartless Scot eggs on a nationalist politician.
annotation.walkthrough: The SNP is the Scottish National Party; Nicola Sturgeon led it and was Scotland's First Minister.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Nicola Sturgeon led the Scottish National Party from 2014 to 2023.

entries.clue: The author’s entering one worried candidate (7)

indicatorNotes.entering: whatever enters something goes inside it, so MINE goes into the next piece
indicatorNotes.worried: a worried thing is agitated and churned up, so the letters of ONE are jumbled

blocks.note: ONE rearranged, split around the insertion
the setter speaking of himself: 'the author's' = mine

annotation.surface: The writer joins a nervous contender in the race.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The author' is the setter, so 'the author's' is the possessive MINE, not I'M.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone formally put forward for an election or award is standing as a candidate.

entries.clue: Farewell from university following a pass (5)

indicatorNotes.following: what follows comes after, so U goes at the end

blocks.note: as it stands
to pass away is to die
u = university

annotation.surface: A student says goodbye to university after scraping a pass.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pass' sounds like an exam grade, but it is the verb meaning die.
annotation.definitionFit: Borrowed word: French for 'to God', used in English as a formal goodbye.

entries.clue: To start with, scouting contingent walking and climbing (10)

indicatorNotes.To start with: a word's start is its first letter, so take the openings of the next two words

blocks.note: first letters of 'scouting' and 'contingent'
rambling = walking in the countryside

annotation.surface: A troop of scouts sets off hiking and clambering over hills.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Walking and climbing' reads as a pair, but only 'walking' is wordplay; 'climbing' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: scrambling is clambering over rough rock using hands as well as feet.

entries.clue: Military officer organised air bridge (9)

indicatorNotes.organised: to organise things is to arrange them into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: An army officer sets up an airlift.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface fits the answer neatly, since organising an air bridge is just the job an officer would do.
annotation.definitionFit: Rank: in the army a brigadier commands a brigade, ranking above colonel.

entries.clue: Join RAC finally on roadside? (8)

indicatorNotes.finally: what comes finally is last, so take the last letter of 'RAC'

blocks.note: last letter of RAC
used as it stands
the verge is the grass strip at the side of a road

annotation.surface: Sign up with the RAC, a British motoring breakdown club, once stranded at the roadside.
annotation.walkthrough: The RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British breakdown service, which makes the roadside feel natural.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: roads or rivers that converge come together and meet at one point.

entries.clue: Agents at ground stand still (8)

indicatorNotes.ground: the past tense of grind: something ground has been crushed and broken up

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: Secret agents at a football ground are told to freeze.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a sports venue, but it is the past tense of grind.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: water that stagnates stops flowing, and an economy that does makes no progress.

entries.clue: Get the better of unfashionable humorist (6)

blocks.note: out = out of fashion
a wit is a clever, funny person

annotation.surface: Someone scores off a comedian who has gone out of style.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pits someone against a humorist, and the answer's own second half is that humorist.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to beat an opponent through cleverness rather than strength.

entries.clue: Retreat after retirement to Venetian location (6)

indicatorNotes.after retirement: to retire is to draw back, so after retirement the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a lair is a hiding place or retreat
used as it stands

annotation.surface: A pensioner withdraws to a spot in Venice.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as moving to Venice after retiring from work; 'retirement' is really the instruction to reverse LAIR.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a district of Venice by the Grand Canal, famous for its bridge and market.

entries.clue: Passionate artist laid up with depression (6)

indicatorNotes.laid up: in a down answer, something laid up is set upward, so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: RA = Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
a dent is a hollow or depression

annotation.surface: An emotional painter is bedridden and depressed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Laid up' and 'depression' suggest an ill, gloomy artist; in fact the depression is a hollow in a surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: from Latin for burning, it describes feelings held with fiery enthusiasm.

entries.clue: Eating, rave about having no meat (10)

indicatorNotes.about: letters turned about have been moved round into a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: Someone enthuses about dining without meat.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder is itself about food, so the whole clue stays on topic.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a diet or dish free of flesh, fish and fowl is called this.

entries.clue: Insult in pub borne by British (4)

indicatorNotes.borne by: in a down answer, what is borne by something is carried on top of it

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
b = British

annotation.surface: A British drinker has to put up with an insult in the pub.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Borne by' reads as putting up with the insult; in a down answer it puts BAR above B.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative: like the hooked point on an arrow, a cutting remark sticks and hurts.

entries.clue: Crack shot’s first to plug jumbo? (4)

indicatorNotes.first: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only the S of 'shot' is used
indicatorNotes.to plug: a plug fills a hole, so S goes inside the next word

blocks.note: a jumbo is a jumbo jet
first letter of 'shot'

annotation.surface: A sharpshooter puts a bullet into an elephant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crack shot' reads as one phrase for a marksman; 'crack' is the definition, a joke, and 'jumbo' is the aircraft, not the elephant.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a crack, as in wisecrack, is a quick witty remark made for laughs.

entries.clue: Come to religious lesson at a church (5)

indicatorNotes.at: something at a place is right beside it, so the pieces follow on

blocks.note: RE = religious education, a school subject
as it stands
ch = church

annotation.surface: An invitation to come to Sunday school at a church.
annotation.walkthrough: RE is religious education, the name British schools give to lessons about faith.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: travellers who arrive at a destination have got there.

entries.clue: Long-handled device regularly used in The Open (3)

indicatorNotes.regularly used in: things happening regularly come at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: t(H)e (O)p(E)n: second, fourth and sixth letters

annotation.surface: A long-handled club gets plenty of use at golf's Open Championship.
annotation.walkthrough: The Open is golf's British Open Championship, so a long-handled device sounds like a putter.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: a garden tool with a flat blade on a long shaft, used for weeding.

entries.clue: Missing golf, move abroad — somewhere like Dubai? (7)

indicatorNotes.Missing: a word missing a letter has lost it, so G is taken out

blocks.note: to emigrate is to move abroad
Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet; removed

annotation.surface: Someone relocates overseas to Dubai, giving up their golf.
annotation.walkthrough: Dubai is one of the seven emirates of the United Arab Emirates.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a state ruled by an emir, and Dubai is one of seven in the UAE.

entries.clue: Steelmen starting late forged iron? (7)

indicatorNotes.starting late: a word that starts late has missed its start, so the first letter goes
indicatorNotes.forged: metal that is forged is hammered into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: STEELMEN loses its first letter S

annotation.surface: Steelworkers who clocked on late hammered out some iron.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark shows iron is an example: it is one element among many.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: iron sits in the periodic table, chemical symbol Fe.

entries.clue: Argue against Root being withdrawn (5)

indicatorNotes.being withdrawn: something withdrawn is pulled back, so the word reads in reverse

blocks.note: a tuber is a swollen root, like a potato

annotation.surface: Someone protests Joe Root, the England cricketer, being taken off.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital R makes Root look like the cricketer, but it is an ordinary root.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to rebut a claim is to contradict it with evidence or counterargument.
